## Bottom line
**Suggests InSitu (86%)** · Confident · Read in turn
Single-class 90% conformal set [F1] (0% invasive risk) on an unflagged Tier 1 simulated frozen section.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | InSitu 86%, Benign 12%, Normal 1%, Invasive 0% | Strong InSitu lead over Benign |
| Conformal set | InSitu (alpha=0.10, 90% coverage, n=132) | Single class at 90% dataset guarantee |
| Reliability / OOD | 98% reliability, 100% OOD, JPEG-3 [F6] | High reliability despite atypical OOD |
| CONCH–MUSK agreement | Agree | Both foundation models match top class |
| Similar cases | 60% (3/5 InSitu, 2/5 Benign) [F5] | Moderate match; two Benign neighbors |

## Tissue evidence
- **Dense lymphocytic infiltrate (TILs)** (regions 0, 4, 8) · context · Above typical (-0.97) [F2]; AI spot check 8/20 · Weak
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 1) · ↓ invasive · Below typical (-0.42) [F3]; scarce invasion, spot check 19/20 · Validated
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (regions 5, 6, 9) · ↓ invasive · Above typical (-0.41) [F4]; duct-confined, spot check 12/20 · Weak
- **Frequent mitotic figures** (region 11) · ↓ invasive · Below typical (-0.37); failed spot check (0/20), ignore · Unreliable

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Faithful; top-3 risk deletion beats random (+0.0114, 95% CI 0.0021–0.0197, n=132).
- **Concepts**: Unproven faithfulness (deletion +0.0008, 95% CI -0.0088–0.0064); uses unreliable mitoses, normal lobules, necrosis.

## Could be wrong if
- **Benign mimic**: Benign is 12% and 2/5 neighbors are Benign (BACH_0226, BACH_0230), separated by weak lymphocyte and unreliable necrosis scores.
- **Focal invasion or margin**: Region 1 has 50% invasive risk; medial/superior/inferior margins hit 91%–95% [F7] without stains.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 1, 7, 11**: Highest invasive risk (50%, 15%, 16%); rule out focal stromal invasion.
2. **Regions 5, 6, 9**: Peak duct-confined scores; confirm in situ versus benign mimic (BACH_0226).
3. **Regions 0, 1, 4, 10**: Check medial (95%), superior (93%), inferior (91%) margins called clear.
